source: Independent right-handed Cartesian matrix arithmetic; no production rotation output used as expected data.

coordinateConvention.angles: longitude first, latitude second, in degrees
coordinateConvention.handedness: right-handed; positive active rotations; column vectors
coordinateConvention.basisMapping: The current reconstruction-core lonLatToUnitVector and Cesium world axes match this oracle basis, so B=I and R_project=B*R_oracle*inverse(B). No Unity left-handed/Y-up axis swap is applied.
coordinateConvention.quaternionMapping: Project fields are {w,x,y,z}; Cesium constructor arguments are (x,y,z,w). This is component reordering, not a spatial change of basis.

derivation: Let s=1/sqrt(2). Source longitude0 latitude45 has vector p=(s,0,s).
Moving plate 101 has Rz(+90): (x,y,z)->(-y,x,z), hence R_moving*p=(0,s,s).
Anchor 102 has Rx(+90). Its inverse Rx(-90): (x,y,z)->(x,z,-y). Apply after the moving rotation: R_anchor^-1*R_moving*p=(0,s,-s).
atan2(y,x)=90 degrees and asin(z)=-45 degrees, giving expected longitude90 latitude-45.
The deliberately wrong order applies Rx(-90) first: p->(s,s,0), then Rz(+90)->(-s,s,0), giving longitude135 latitude0.
Both longitude and latitude differ by45 degrees between correct and reversed results, far above tolerance. The original common-axis north-pole examples cannot detect this order reversal.
validationScope: Parser, RotationModel and Cesium matrix conversion can be checked against these independent numbers. This is not GPU/browser validation or final scientific acceptance.
